references.title: A Diffusion Theory Model of Adoption and Substitution for Successive Generations of High-Technology Products
references.supports: Attribution and scope of the successive-generation diffusion model.
references.limits: The full 1987 paper was not inspected; this source does not qualify the repository implementation or its generalized variants.

references.title: When Should Nintendo Launch its Wii? Insights From a Bivariate Successive Generation Model
references.supports: The two-generation level equations and transfer interpretation used in the independent analytic example.
references.limits: Does not validate numerical recovery, arbitrary generation counts, or the empirical fit of these examples.

references.title: Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: An improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC
references.supports: At least four chains, a 1.01 R-hat first-level check, and quantity-specific effective sample size and Monte Carlo error assessment.
references.limits: Diagnostic thresholds do not prove convergence or validate the observation model; the example's 1.05 assertion is only a fixture regression tolerance.

references.title: Exact testing with random permutations
references.supports: Group invariance under the null as the basis of exact transformation tests, including sign transformations.
references.limits: Does not establish sign exchangeability for the supplied study, independent information from duplicated pairs, or confidence-interval coverage.

references.title: Double/Debiased Machine Learning for Treatment and Causal Parameters
references.supports: The roles of orthogonal scores and cross-fitting in separating nuisance estimation from target-parameter estimation.
references.limits: Only the abstract was inspected for this claim; it does not establish causal identification or finite-sample coverage for Innovate's stratum-mean estimator.

references.title: Constructing Inverse Probability Weights for Marginal Structural Models
references.supports: Substantive requirements of consistency, exchangeability and positivity for a causal interpretation.
references.limits: Does not validate the implementation's AIPW variance, remove confounding, or justify assumptions for a synthetic or empirical diffusion study.

findings.finding: Opening wording attributed scientific validation to the Rust implementation.
findings.resolution: Separated request/domain/operation validation from model, data and study-design validity.

findings.finding: Readers needed a common interpretation of levels, rates, time units and population denominators.
findings.resolution: Added task routing and a units/denominators table; distinguished level change, interval average rate, derivative and unique adoption.

findings.finding: A noiseless model-generated recovery and held-out prediction example could be mistaken for external validation.
findings.resolution: Identified the synthetic generating process, independent algebraic oracle and bounds on empirical inference.

findings.finding: The guide retained stale counts and said implemented helpers and IPC wrappers were unavailable.
findings.resolution: Removed fixed obligation/fitter counts and obsolete dependency versions, linked current references, and described implemented extensions with remaining qualification limits.

findings.finding: The scalar posterior and diagnostic threshold needed explicit scale conventions and an interpretation boundary.
findings.resolution: Derived posterior precision and mean; distinguished API standard deviations from mathematical variances, conditional posterior uncertainty from Monte Carlo/model uncertainty, and the fixture threshold from primary diagnostic guidance.

findings.finding: Exact enumeration could be misread as proof of study assumptions or interval coverage.
findings.resolution: Explained null invariance, descriptive intervals and duplicated-pair limits.

findings.finding: Cross-fitting and counterfactual forecast operations needed clearer separation from empirical identification.
findings.resolution: Added AIPW score arithmetic, the 5.25 outcome-unit mean, nuisance-model scope, support and interference considerations, small-sample limits, and conditional forecast interpretation.

findings.finding: A checksum description could imply whole-artifact authenticity.
findings.resolution: Specified sorted serialized dataset coverage and the extraction_time/checksum exclusions; distinguished content integrity from authenticated authorship, rights and scientific validity.

findings.finding: A predict-only example called query times observations and lacked interpretation exercises.
findings.resolution: Corrected the term and added worked level-change, unit-conversion and slope questions, explicitly separate from executed assertions.

findings.finding: Different scenarios, denominators and evaluation times could be ranked as a common policy effect.
findings.resolution: Added a scenario input/output table, horizon and hazard explanations, matched-comparison questions and identification limits.

reader_tasks.prompt: Distinguish the prediction at time 1 from the increase between times 0 and 1.
reader_tasks.expected_answer: Level 50; interval increase approximately 23.105858 adoption units.

reader_tasks.prompt: Convert years to months while preserving the same Logistic curve.
reader_tasks.expected_answer: Multiply time and x0 by 12, divide k by 12, keep L unchanged.

reader_tasks.prompt: Derive the instantaneous Logistic slope at the midpoint and identify its units.
reader_tasks.expected_answer: L*k/4 = 25 adoption units per year; differs from a level or whole-interval change.

reader_tasks.prompt: Explain why the pause fixture has no adoption and when the argument would fail.
reader_tasks.expected_answer: Innovation, imitation and initial adopters are zero; another mechanism invalidates this argument.

reader_tasks.prompt: Calculate year-two incumbent and entrant levels and identify the denominator.
Assess whether comparing year-two replacement to year-five baseline answers the intervention question.
reader_tasks.expected_answer: It does not answer the intervention contrast; model, outcome and time differ.

reader_tasks.prompt: Reconcile standard-deviation API inputs with the scalar posterior variance and mean.
reader_tasks.expected_answer: Posterior precision is 1/4+(1/2)^2 = 1/2; posterior variance is 2 and mean is 98 before truncation.

reader_tasks.prompt: Explain what a minimum treated/control count demonstrates and which identification questions remain.
reader_tasks.expected_answer: An observed count; not exchangeability, suitable interference assumptions or calibrated precision.
